Anaphylaxis: two or more of skin or mucosal involvement, respiratory compromise, persistent GI symptoms, hypotension or its symptoms, rapidly after a likely allergen (skin absent in up to 40%). Epinephrine is the primary treatment: 1 mg/mL IM in the anterolateral thigh, 0.3 mg at 25 kg or more, 0.15 mg under 25 kg, from a vial or auto-injector; repeat every 5-15 minutes if anaphylaxis and hypoperfusion persist; albuterol for wheeze; 20 mL/kg isotonic fluid IV or IO for hypoperfusion (ALS); time to epinephrine is a safety consideration.

sources.cite: NHTSA. National EMS Scope of Practice Model 2019 (DOT HS 812 666), with Change Notices 1.0 and 2.0 (2021)
sources.note: Read 2026-11-11 in a text extraction of the Louisiana copy (the extractor did not keep every table column, so placement was checked against the course's own reading of 2026-11-09 in ems-sources.ts). EMR: CPR and AED, tourniquet and wound packing, naloxone, oral airway, BVM, oxygen; no pulse oximetry, glucose monitoring, epinephrine auto-injector or transport. EMT adds pulse oximetry, glucose monitoring, epinephrine auto-injector, aspirin, oral glucose, CPAP, 12-lead acquisition (not interpretation), transport. AEMT adds IV and IO access, non-medicated IV fluids, supraglottic airways and a limited list of IV and IM medications including dextrose and glucagon. Paramedic adds 12-lead interpretation, manual defibrillation, intubation and the wider formulary. No newer model was found 2026-11-11 (EMS.gov's page was unavailable; the only other 'update' found is the 2017 change notice adding tourniquets, wound packing and naloxone to EMR and EMT).

brief.situation: 19:20. You and your partner are EMTs on an ambulance, called to a restaurant. Maya, 22, about 60 kg, ate a dish with peanut sauce about 10 minutes ago at a birthday dinner. She says her throat feels tight and she feels faint.
handover: Her own auto-injector is at home. Your ambulance carries agency epinephrine auto-injectors, adult (0.3 mg) and junior (0.15 mg), oxygen, and her albuterol inhaler is in her bag.
Paramedics can meet you on the way if you ask. The nearest emergency department is about 14 minutes away.
Within EMT scope: epinephrine auto-injector, oxygen, assisting with an inhaled bronchodilator. No IV fluids or IV drugs.
howItWorks: The clock runs in simulated time; study pace runs three simulated seconds per real second. Pause any time.
Scene time and the drive both run on the clock. Treatment continues in the ambulance.
Partway through you are asked to explain your decisions in writing. The case ends at the hospital, then a debrief scores what you did.

source.note: FLAG: stands in for a number no guideline gives. Untreated, this reaction progresses from moderate to cardiovascular collapse in about 8 minutes (under 20 minutes after the exposure). Simplified teaching model written for exam practice; not a validated physiological model.

FLAG: stands in for a number no guideline gives. One adult IM dose reverses the reaction at about 0.15 severity units per minute at its peak. Simplified teaching model written for exam practice; not a validated physiological model.

FLAG: stands in for a number no guideline gives. The IM dose's effect wanes with a 5-minute time constant, so hypoperfusion returns about 15 minutes later in this case; NASEMSO's repeat interval is 5-15 minutes. Simplified teaching model written for exam practice; not a validated physiological model.

FLAG: stands in for a number no guideline gives. An IM dose in the deltoid acts less than one in the anterolateral thigh; NASEMSO specifies the thigh. Simplified teaching model written for exam practice; not a validated physiological model.

FLAG: stands in for a number no guideline gives. Walking a hypotensive anaphylaxis patient upright can precipitate sudden collapse (a sudden fall in venous return). Simplified teaching model written for exam practice; not a validated physiological model.

effects.log: Peanut allergy (anaphylaxis at 15); mild asthma, albuterol inhaler; no other medications. Peanut sauce about 10 minutes before the call; throat tight within minutes, vomited once.
Cuff, pulse oximeter, count the breaths (about 1 min).

why.question: What makes this anaphylaxis rather than a mild allergic reaction, and what will tell you she needs a second dose?

parts.label: Recognition
parts.criteria: Skin and mucosal signs plus respiratory compromise (hoarseness, throat tightness, wheeze) and hypotension or faintness, minutes after a known allergen: anaphylaxis, so epinephrine IM at once; hives alone would be a mild reaction.
parts.modelAnswer: Hives and lip swelling plus a hoarse voice, throat tightness and wheeze, and a low blood pressure with faintness, minutes after peanut: two or more systems, so anaphylaxis, not a skin-only reaction. Epinephrine IM in the thigh now.

parts.label: Reassessment and the repeat dose
parts.criteria: Reassess airway, breathing, pulse and blood pressure every few minutes; repeat the dose 5-15 minutes after the first if hypoperfusion or respiratory compromise persists or returns; keep her flat, do not let her walk; oxygen; paramedics for IV fluids.
parts.modelAnswer: Recheck her breathing, pulse and blood pressure every few minutes. If she is still hypotensive or the signs return 5-15 minutes after the first dose, give a second dose. Keep her flat, never walk her, oxygen, and ask paramedics for IV fluids.

noProgress.rationale: She reaches the hospital alive but still hypotensive: treatment helped too little or too late. This case calls it recovered, not target.

expertPath.text: Hoarse, wheezing, hives and swollen lips, faint, minutes after peanut: anaphylaxis. Check the adult auto-injector; 0.3 mg IM into the outer thigh.
Flat with legs raised, oxygen, vital signs (BP 86/52), SAMPLE history. Request a paramedic intercept.
Onto the stretcher lying flat and go; notify the hospital. Albuterol for the wheeze if it persists.
Faintness back, BP below 90: second 0.3 mg IM. Paramedic adds IV fluid. Reassess every few minutes.

arrest.headline: She collapsed
arrest.body: Anaphylaxis can move from hives to collapse in minutes. Epinephrine IM in the thigh is the treatment; antihistamines, inhalers and watching are not. Look at when the first dose went in and whether she was walked.

stable.headline: At the hospital, improving
stable.body: Early recognition, the right dose in the right site, a flat patient, and a second dose as soon as the pressure fell again. That is the expert path.

arrived.headline: Arrived, by a harder route
arrived.body: She made it, but check the first dose (when, which auto-injector, where), whether the second dose came when the pressure fell, and how she got to the ambulance.

scoring.modelReasoning: Hives and lip swelling with throat tightness, hoarseness, wheeze and a low blood pressure minutes after a known allergen is anaphylaxis, not a mild reaction. Epinephrine is the primary treatment: check the auto-injector, then 0.3 mg IM into the anterolateral thigh for a patient of 25 kg or more, at once. Lay her flat with legs raised and never walk her; oxygen; vital signs; ask for paramedics for IV fluids. Reassess every few minutes; if hypoperfusion persists or returns 5-15 minutes after the dose, repeat it. Albuterol helps the wheeze only. Scene time counts: load her lying flat, notify the hospital, and keep treating en route.

mild.ask: While the vital signs cycle: which finding alone would make this a mild allergic reaction rather than anaphylaxis?

choices.label: Hives only, with normal breathing and blood pressure
Hives with faintness and a low blood pressure

mild.explain: Signs in one organ system (hives alone) are a non-anaphylactic reaction. Skin signs with respiratory compromise or hypotension, rapidly after an allergen, are anaphylaxis.

repeatQ.ask: On the way: when would you give a second epinephrine dose?

choices.label: 5-15 minutes after the first if hypoperfusion or breathing trouble persists or returns
Never: one dose is the EMT limit

repeatQ.explain: NASEMSO: repeat the IM dose every 5-15 minutes while anaphylaxis with hypoperfusion persists. Reassess every few minutes so you notice when it returns.
